# Results — Study 820 (Expected-Shortfall Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — a priced
downside **tail-risk premium**: stocks whose recent daily returns have a fat left tail (a
large trailing **Expected Shortfall** / CVaR at 5%, the mean of the worst 5% of days) are
riskier, so if tail risk is compensated they should earn **more**; a long-high-ES /
short-low-ES book should earn a positive spread. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-252-day historical Expected Shortfall** (CVaR) at 5% — the negative mean of the worst `ceil(0.05·252)=13` daily returns, a positive magnitude (larger = fatter left tail), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the top 30%** (high ES, fat tail), **short the bottom 30%** (low ES), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled high-vs-low books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. This bias
cuts *toward* the result: the names that survived to be mega-caps today (NVDA, TSLA, AMD, …)
are exactly the high-tail-risk winners of 2010–2026, so a high-ES-earns-more sort is flattered
by construction. Read the stamp below with that in mind.

## The headline — long-high-ES / short-low-ES spread

Daily equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% Expected-Shortfall spread (n = **3,894** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long high-ES − short low-ES)** | **+5.41 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+2.80** |
| one-sample *t* | +2.71 |
| high-ES book / low-ES book | +10.43 bps / +5.03 bps (Welch *t* = +1.84) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | +0.69 |

The claimed sign **holds**: on this liquid mega-cap tape the fat-left-tail (high-ES) names
went on to out-earn the thin-tail (low-ES) names by **+5.41 bps/day** with a Newey-West
*t* = **+2.80** — a genuine positive on the real tape. Two large caveats travel with it. First,
Expected Shortfall is ~collinear with total volatility (it reads the *depth* of the worst days),
so this is essentially a **long-high-vol / short-low-vol** sort — the *opposite* of the classic
low-volatility anomaly (study 501), which won here only because the surviving high-vol mega-caps
(the momentum tech complex) were the decade's winners. Second, the pooled book test is only
Welch *t* = +1.84 (< 2), so the edge lives in the *tails* of the cross-section, not the median.

## Placebo — is the relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-ES sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted** panel
(signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+5.41 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.072 bps (1.147) |
| position of observed | ≈ **+4.78σ into the right tail** (right-tail p ≈ 0.000) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed +5.41 bps sits far in the **right** tail, so
the relation is not a lucky sort — the high-ES names really did earn more on this universe.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,760) | +3.86 bps | +1.67 |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +6.68 bps | **+2.26** |

The premium is **era-dependent**: it is clearly significant only in the 2018–2026 half (the
NVDA/TSLA/AMD melt-up) and merely a positive tilt (*t* = +1.67, not significant on its own) in
2010–2017. This is the honest fingerprint of a **survivor-and-regime** effect rather than a
stable priced premium.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +5.41 bps | 2.14 bps | **+3.27 bps** | +1.64 | +0.42 | +8.2%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +5.41 bps | 10.14 bps | **−4.73 bps** | −2.37 | −0.60 | −11.9%/yr |

At an optimistic **1 bp** one-way the book nets **+3.27 bps/day** (~+8%/yr, Sharpe 0.42) — but
the net *t* is only **+1.64** (< 2), so even the friendliest cost leaves no *robust* net edge.
At a realistic **5 bps** the round-trip friction (10.14 bps/day) swamps the gross edge and the
book turns **significantly negative** (−4.73 bps/day, *t* = −2.37). No robust paycheck survives.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent "tail loading" that fattens each name's left
tail and (with `edge>0`) *raises* its forward mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.03** (sd 0.97), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** (≈ the nominal 5% rate) |
| planted (`edge = 0.0024`, seed 820) | **+3.54** (Welch *t* = +3.64) |

The detector recovers a *planted* tail-risk premium cleanly and is unbiased on the null (mean
*t* ≈ 0, false-positive rate ≈ nominal) — so the positive real-tape result is a property of the
data, not of the machinery. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of
the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK (a flattered near-miss).** The claimed downside tail-risk premium **replicates in
  sign** on 50 liquid US mega-caps: the long-high-ES / short-low-ES spread is **+5.41 bps/day**
  (NW *t* = **+2.80**, ≈+4.8σ over a 1,000-permutation placebo). But it is **era-dependent**
  (significant only post-2018, *t* = +1.67 / +2.26), the pooled book test is sub-threshold
  (Welch *t* = +1.84), and — because Expected Shortfall is ~collinear with volatility on a
  **survivor** universe — it is most honestly read as the surviving high-vol tech mega-caps
  winning the 2018–2026 melt-up, i.e. the *inverse* of the low-vol anomaly, not a clean priced
  tail premium. Robust by the headline *t*, fragile in mechanism.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** At 1 bp one-way the book nets +3.27 bps/day (~+8%/yr) but with net
  *t* = +1.64 (not robust); at a realistic 5 bps it is **−4.73 bps/day** (*t* = −2.37). The gross
  edge is real but too thin to survive realistic friction.
